items.requirement: tsrs checks and emits TSX (react-jsx) against virtual node_modules declarations for React and a custom SDK package, from an in-memory file map
evidence: Node run of @tsrs/wasm 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta, 2026-11-10: exit 0 on a valid file, TS2339 and TS2345 on the planted errors, about 260 ms cold, 111 MiB. Not yet run in a browser worker.

items.requirement: A rustyred-wasm crate in RustyRedDB builds the graph store over the OPFS projection chunk store and over memory, without Database::create/open
@rustyreddb/browser mirrors the Node binding (mutate, getNode, getEdge, queryNodes, neighbors, query, fulltext, compact, close) with the same error codes, behind an async client that owns the worker
subscribe re-runs a registered read after a commit and posts the result
Headless Chromium: records written are read back after a page reload; runtime panics on wasm32 found by this run are fixed
A db capability is declared like the others and db.* page methods are parsed and checked against it
One database per App document id in a host-page worker; every revision of an App sees the same records; a pinned revision is read-only
window.theorem.db in the app bridge, with subscriptions delivered over the existing port
An App can be several source files in its document; the single-HTML form still works
esbuild-wasm builds a source revision against the import map; a failed build keeps the last working preview
tsrs checks the same frozen snapshot in its own worker, loaded on first use; results for a superseded revision are dropped
Declarations for @theorem/app are generated from the bridge schemas
The frame forwards error and unhandledrejection with source-mapped positions
Build errors, check diagnostics and runtime errors reach the agent as a repair reference naming the source revision
The Theorem builder can emit the multi-file App form (Theorem repo)
Checker load, memory and time measured on a phone
Build-time element ids and an id to source-span index per revision; ids never written into source
Reversible actions (property, token or style, insert, reorder, remove, binding, extract) become AST edits against the revision they were made on
Component plugins and style books are vault folders with manifest, declarations, inventory, schema-checked tokens and a usage file
A component saved from the designer can be imported by another App
A vault module is editable with the TypeScript path and the designer and updates on a page without reloading the host
